items.prompt: White to move. One rook move gives check, and it is checkmate. Find it.
hints: Look at the black king and the three pawns in front of it. Which row is the king standing on?
Your rook is on the e-file with an open road to the top. Which square on the back row could it reach?
Slide the rook straight up the e-file to the eighth row.
items.explain: The rook slides up the open e-file and checks along the back row. Black's own pawns fill f7, g7 and h7, so the king has no square, and nothing can capture the rook or block. Checkmate.

items.prompt: Black is checkmated. Tap each square beside the black king that is blocked by one of Black's own pieces.

claims.statement: A black pawn stands on f7.
A black pawn stands on g7.
A black pawn stands on h7.

hints: The king is on g8. Look at the row just below it.
Three squares in that row are occupied by Black's own pieces.
They hold the three pawns, f7, g7 and h7.
items.explain: The three pawns in front of the king fill f7, g7 and h7. A king may not move onto a square holding its own piece, and the rook covers the back row, so the king has no move at all.

items.prompt: White plays the rook to d8, giving check. Is it checkmate? Predict, then check.

claims.statement: Rd8 is legal and gives check.
Rd8 is check but not checkmate.

hints: After Rd8+, which of Black's pieces can move to a square between the rook and the king?
The black bishop on c6 looks along a diagonal. Where does that diagonal end?
The bishop can move to e8, between the rook and the king.
items.explain: The bishop on c6 slides to e8 and stands between the rook and the king. A check that can be blocked is not checkmate, so White has only given check.

items.prompt: White plays the rook to d8, giving check. Is it checkmate? Predict, then check.
hints: Check each answer in turn: can the king step, can the rook be taken, can something block?
Where could the black bishop go that lies between d8 and g8?
The bishop on e6 reaches neither e8 nor f8.
items.explain: The bishop on e6 looks like a possible blocker, but none of its moves reaches e8 or f8, the squares between the rook and the king. The king has no square and nothing can capture the rook. Checkmate.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a checkmate in one.
hints: Your king on c7 already covers some of the squares near the black king. Which ones?
The queen must give check. A move that leaves the king untouched is not mate.
Several queen moves give check; any one of them leaves the king no square. Beware: one queen move leaves Black with no legal move and no check, which is stalemate.
items.explain: Black's king on a8 has only a7, b7 and b8 to go to. Your king covers b7 and b8, so a queen that checks and covers a7 finishes it. The queen move to b6 does not give check, so it is not a mate.

feedback_by_move.b1b6: The queen on b6 covers the squares around the king but does not give check. That cannot be checkmate: checkmate needs a check.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a checkmate in one? If so, play it.
hints: List every check first. Then ask the three questions about each one.
Two of the checks lose the queen at once. Which black pieces can capture her?
The queen reaches the back row on a square that no black piece can attack.
items.explain: Qe8 gives check along the back row. The knight on c6 cannot take on e8 and cannot reach f8, so nothing captures or blocks, and the pawns shut the king in. The other checks fail: the knight takes on d8, and the king takes on f7.

feedback_by_move.d7d8: The knight on c6 captures the queen on d8. A check that can be captured is not checkmate, and it costs the queen.
feedback_by_move.d7f7: The king takes the queen on f7, because nothing defends that square. A queen next to the king needs a defender.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a checkmate in one.
hints: Which white pawn is guarded only by the king?
Two of your pieces aim at f2. One of them gives the check, the other defends it.
The queen takes on f2; the bishop on c5 defends her.
items.explain: The queen takes the pawn on f2 and the bishop on c5 defends that square, so the white king cannot take the queen. The king's own pieces block its other squares. Checkmate.

feedback_by_move.c5f2: The bishop takes with check, but the king takes the bishop. Only the queen, defended by the bishop, gives checkmate.

items.prompt: It is Black's turn. What mate does White threaten if Black ignores it?

claims.statement: If Black passes, Re8 is checkmate.

hints: Which of White's pieces looks at the back row?
The rook is on the e-file. Where would it check?
The rook would go to e8.
items.explain: White's rook threatens to go to e8. With the pawns in front of the king, that would be checkmate, so Black must make a square for the king or cover the back row first.

items.prompt: White to move. Is there a checkmate in one? Predict, then check.
hints: Your king is far away. Which squares near the black king does it cover?
Take any queen check, for example next to the king. What can the black king do?
The king simply captures an undefended queen or steps to a free square.
items.explain: Every check can be answered. Next to the king the queen is undefended and is captured; from a distance the king keeps a free square. With nothing to help the queen, there is no checkmate.

items.prompt: White to move. Find a checkmate in one.
hints: Your king on f7 covers g8 and g7. Which squares are left for the black king?
The queen must give check and stand where the king cannot take her.
Qg7 is next to the king, and your king defends it.
items.explain: The white king covers g7 and g8, so Black's king has only h7 to run to. A queen that gives check and also covers h7 mates, and the king guards her where she stands next to Black's king.

feedback_by_move.g1g6: The queen on g6 covers the squares around the king but gives no check. Black has no legal move and the game is a draw by stalemate, not a win.

items.prompt: White to move. Is Ra8 checkmate? Predict, then check.
hints: Where could the king step after the check?
Count the king's neighbours: which are free?
items.explain: The pawns on f7, g7 and h7 fill the squares in front of the king, and the rook covers f8 and h8. No step, no capture, no block: checkmate.

items.prompt: White to move. Is Ra8 checkmate? Predict, then check.
hints: Which square did the pawn leave free?
Where does the king go after Ra8+?
items.explain: The pawn on h6 left h7 free. After Ra8+ the king steps to h7, so it is check, not mate.
